title: Piano lessons from the rooming-house pianist; bass came later
summary: The roomer gave him his first piano lessons, scales and chords, though piano was not his bag; the bass came around 1935.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was just saying that they've reported you as having studied some piano, and so what time was that then?
When you were staying in the rooming house.
And this fellow could play some piano.
Right, he played very good piano.
He would sit you down at the piano, then?
And he started me out, learning to play the piano, yeah. Like your first lesson, (singing).
Oh, he did? He put you on some scales.
And I enjoyed it, but it just wasn't my bag, as you say.
But did he have a feeling for jazz?
Well, that was pretty good, then.
I can't think of his name. I wish I could think of it. My mother would remember that.
Well, anyway, that gave you an idea of where the notes lay on the piano.
He showed me exactly -- from C, and --
Yeah. And you realized that was in a clef with a bass and all that.
Well, now, also it was reported that you studied the bass.
